lines.text: This is your token board book. Four laminated pages are bound on the left, with a tab for each: Choices, Targets, Board, and Tokens.
lines.screen: The closed book lies on a table with its four labelled tabs showing on the right, then it opens to the first page.

lines.text: Page one is the Choices page. Show it before the task begins. Every picture should be something your learner values right now, not something they can get any time, or have just had plenty of.
lines.screen: The Choices page fills the frame, with six choice cards on its six boxes.

lines.text: Your learner looks over the pictures and picks one to work for. If needed, help with the pointing, but let your learner make the choice.
lines.screen: The learner's small hand moves across the cards, points at one, then pinches it and lifts it off the page.

lines.text: Page two is the Targets page, where you choose what to teach: a new skill, or a better way to get what a problem behavior was getting.
lines.screen: The page turns to the Targets page, with six teaching target cards on its boxes.

lines.text: Choose one target at a time. Agree with the other adults on exactly what counts, so everyone gives tokens for the same thing.
lines.screen: The teacher's hand, with a shirt cuff, picks the target card and lifts it off the page.

lines.text: Page three is the Board. Place the target under First, and the chosen item under Then. Your learner can now see the plan: first the target, then the item.
lines.screen: The page turns to the Board; the target card goes into the First box and the chosen item card into the Then box, and each box glows as the plan is named.

lines.text: Page four is the Tokens page, where the tokens wait. The empty slots on the board show your learner how many are left to earn. Make new tokens valuable first; the tips at the end show how.
lines.screen: The Tokens page appears beside the Board with its tokens in their boxes, and the empty token slots on the Board are highlighted.

lines.text: Before you start, decide how much of the target behavior earns a token: how many times, or how long. Keep it small, so your learner can succeed. This example uses one token for every two minutes.
lines.screen: A note over the Board and Tokens page reads: one token for every two minutes of the target behavior.

lines.text: Now start the session. Point to the board and name both pictures: first the target, then the item. The ring counts down each two-minute interval, sped up for this video.
lines.screen: The teacher's hand points to the First card, then the Then card; a timer ring labelled as sped up appears beside the Board and counts down from 2:00.

lines.text: The interval is over, and your learner kept up the target behavior the whole time. Give a token right away, with brief praise that names what they did. Your learner places it in the first slot.
lines.screen: As the ring completes, the teacher's hand takes a token from the Tokens page and holds it out with a speech bubble of praise that names the target; the learner's hand puts it in the first slot.

lines.text: If the behavior stops during an interval, give no token, but leave the earned tokens on the board. Calmly remind your learner what to do, and start the next interval.
lines.screen: The ring completes without the behavior; no token moves, a note says no token this interval and the earned tokens stay, and the ring starts again.

lines.text: Each interval with the target behavior earns another token, given right away with a few words of praise. The board fills up, one slot at a time.
lines.screen: The intervals run faster now; token after token goes into the next slot, each with a short bubble of praise.

lines.text: One more interval earns the last token. It looks different: this is the terminal token, earned just like the others. With practice, it tells your learner that the board is finished and the item comes next.
lines.screen: After one more interval the teacher's hand holds out the last token, with its own picture and an orange double border; the learner's hand puts it in the last slot, which carries an orange ring.

lines.text: One more interval with the target behavior, and the last token goes in. Now the board is full, and your learner has earned the item they chose.
lines.screen: After one more interval the last token goes into the last slot, and every slot on the Board is full.

lines.text: The board is full, so make the exchange right away, especially while the board is new: your learner gets the Then item, for a time or amount set before the session.
lines.screen: The Then card lifts and grows, and the teacher's hand passes it to the learner's hand, with a label for the time with the item.

lines.text: When the time with the item is up, put the tokens back on the Tokens page, and the pictures back on their pages. After that, your learner chooses again for the next round.
lines.screen: The tokens go back to the Tokens page, the two cards return to their pages, and the book turns back to the Choices page, where the learner's hand points again.

lines.text: Three tips. Make the tokens valuable first: give one and trade it for the item right away, again and again, until your learner reaches for the token. Start with a small requirement and few tokens, and raise them slowly; if the behavior falls apart, go back a step. Keep the item available only through the board.
lines.screen: Three short tips appear one by one beside the book: make the tokens valuable first, start small and raise slowly, the item only through the board.

lines.text: That's the whole cycle: choose, set the target, earn the tokens, and exchange. Over time, the target behavior should happen more often; if not, change the item or the requirement. The back of each page tells you more.
lines.screen: The book closes on the table with its four tabs showing, and the four steps of the cycle appear one by one.
